_comment: Maps the 14 ransomware.live `activity` sector tags to NAICS codes, so victim counts (numerator) can join Census firm counts (denominator). Keyed on ransomware_live_sector because that is the field victim records actually carry. Hand-curated and reviewable; consumed by scripts/fetch_exposure.py.
validation_rules: No NAICS code may be assigned (net of excludes) to more than one sector.
Each sector must resolve to a non-zero denominator.

Do NOT assert the sum of sector firm counts <= the SUSB US total. SUSB counts a firm in every sector it operates in, so the sum of all 20 top-level sectors is 6,461,497 against an unduplicated total of 6,395,635 (1.03% over). Verified 2026-10-01.

sectors.notes: Clean 1:1 with NAICS 62. Note 622 (Hospitals) is only 3,136 firms of the 693,801 - the sector is dominated by small practices, which matters for the size dimension.

supplement.source: NCES Common Core of Data (13,318 public school districts) + IPEDS (~1,600 public degree-granting institutions)
supplement.rationale: SUSB NAICS 61 covers private employer firms only. Public districts and public universities are a large share of observed education victims, so they must be in the denominator.

sectors.notes: Private (SUSB 61) + public (NCES/IPEDS). Public institutions added as a constant, not scraped.

NAICS is the literal range string '31-33' in SUSB, not a 2-digit code. Food (311) and beverage (312) manufacturing are EXCLUDED here and assigned to Agriculture and Food Production, matching the DBIR industry name 'Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production'.
Clean 1:1. Large denominator (782,487) dominated by very small contractors, which pushes the observed rate low.

sectors.industry: Professional, Scientific, Technical Services, Real Estate and Wholesale Trade
sectors.notes: WEAKEST SEGMENT. Spans 5 unrelated NAICS sectors with very different risk profiles: Professional/Scientific/Technical (872,305), Real Estate (366,557 - mostly 1-4 employee landlords and brokers), Wholesale (277,932), Management of Companies (25,413), Admin/Waste (376,192). 5415 (Computer Systems Design) is excluded and assigned to Technology. Report a with/without-NAICS-53 sensitivity; the headline rate for this sector is close to meaningless.

Retail (literal range '44-45') + Other Services (81). NAICS 71 (Arts/Entertainment) is deliberately NOT here - it is assigned to Hospitality, whose DBIR industry name explicitly includes 'Arts and Entertainment'. Large micro-firm-dominated denominator.

A sub-sector composite with no single NAICS home: Software Publishers (5112, 13,674) + Data Processing/Hosting (518, 11,482) + Other Information Services (5191, 10,873) + Computer Systems Design (5415, 127,147). 5415 sits inside NAICS 54 and is excluded from Business Services to avoid double-assignment. 517 (Telecom) deliberately excluded - assigned to Telecommunication.
Small denominator (12,086) makes this the highest observed rate; rate is sensitive to a handful of victims. Report the Poisson CI prominently.
Utilities (22, 6,772) + Mining/Oil & Gas Extraction (21, 17,341). Small denominator; publicly-owned utilities are excluded from SUSB, which understates the denominator and overstates the rate.

sectors.industry: Accommodation, Food Services, Arts and Entertainment
sectors.notes: Accommodation/Food Services (72) + Arts/Entertainment/Recreation (71), matching the DBIR industry name. 71 is assigned here and NOT to Consumer Services.

sectors.industry: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Food Production
sectors.notes: Crop/animal production (11, 22,599) + food mfg (311, 25,675) + beverage mfg (312, 11,382), the latter two excluded from Manufacturing. DELIBERATE CHOICE: USDA NASS counts ~1.9M farms vs SUSB's 22,599, but NASS counts every farm including those with no payroll and no IT estate. Employer firms are the realistic target population; using 1.9M would wrongly dilute the rate ~30x. Recorded as an assumption (A-AGRI-DENOM).

supplement.source: US Census Bureau, 2022 Census of Governments (90,837 local governments: 3,031 counties, 19,429 municipalities, 16,228 townships, 12,546 school districts, 39,603 special districts; plus 50 state governments)
supplement.rationale: NAICS 92 (Public Administration) is absent from SUSB entirely - SUSB covers private employer firms only. Verified: zero rows match NAICS 92.

sectors.notes: DIFFERENT UNIT: governments, not firms. A county is one unit but runs dozens of separately attackable agencies, so this rate is NOT comparable to the firm-based rates and must never share an unlabelled column with them.
